scope: Four isolated 2 m BOX160 cantilevers, eight B32R elements; no full-bridge equilibrium or modal result is established.
independent_method: Read actual DAT displacement rows directly, compare exact input hashes, and evaluate Rodrigues rotation with elementary dot/cross products. Existing native_vectors.json is not used to calculate these checks.

conclusions: All four native computations exit 0, converge in two iterations at the first full-load increment, and print one complete displacement field.
ROTY is 5.025179e-5 rad in all four cases; the current arm and BeamLine free-tip section transfer My without a missing torsional load path.

The offset cases match native Fx plus My in the printed tip X displacement, theta_y and theta_z. Their maximum tip-vector difference is 1.80031446102e-9 m and maximum rotation-vector difference is about 1.797e-9 rad, confined to small finite-geometry components.
Arm and BeamLine offset displacements satisfy independently evaluated finite Rodrigues kinematics to the native DAT rounding scale.

The torsional rotation is only 75.0 percent of the thin-wall Saint-Venant scale, implying approximately 33.3 percent higher effective torsional rigidity for this native beam representation/fixture. This discrepancy already exists in the torque-only case and is therefore not introduced by either offset connector; it remains a separate element/section/warping issue requiring independent section or mesh evidence before claiming accurate physical torsion.
The present checks do not establish the correctness of arbitrary off-mesh section interpolation, the floor-beam rope topology, or full-bridge nonlinear equilibrium.
